column1: # id    Echoes the seed-corpus entry it encodes. Survivor id is `catalog::<id>` —
#       inherently stable, unlike the generic tier's positional ordinals.
# guard Repo-root-relative path of the file the sed mutates. Must be in-universe and
#       must NOT be excluded (the companion selftest lints both).
# sed   A sed -E program applied to the WHOLE guard file.
# note  What regression the mutant models, i.e. what a survivor would MEAN.
# THE LOUD RULE. Unlike a generic mutant, a catalog sed that leaves the file
# byte-identical, or yields `bash -n`-invalid output, is ANCHOR DRIFT = RED. These are
# hand-authored against named sites, so "it no longer applies" is a bug in THIS FILE, not
# "mutation did not apply — the sed anchor has moved" convention.
# PATTERN ADDRESSES ONLY (D-3) — a bare line address is not permitted, and the companion
# selftest rejects one. This is not defensive style: the check-emit-deadline site below
# was verified at :132/:133 during one intake run of this ticket and sits at :200 in the
# base the work branched from, moved by an unrelated PR two merges later. It survived only
# because it was addressed by its expression. A multi-line block uses a start/end pattern
# range. A PR that edits a guard re-anchors that guard's rows in the same diff — the same
# obligation the generic tier has to re-baseline its ordinals.
# SCOPE. Bash guards only. The .mjs / .md / .yml / multi-file corpus entries are deferred
# to #240, and the struck diff-range entry (a future-refactor prediction with nothing to
# sed) stays struck. No corpus line is silently dropped.

column4: Bot silently ENABLED for configs that omit the key — the inverse of the fail-loud posture the helper exists for.
Loosened marker window. No fixture places a marker 40-400 lines above a site and the floor is window-independent, so the clean live tree passes either way.
Deletes an unexercised CHECKS row: coverage silently narrows while every existing injection fixture still passes.
Neuters the planGates (EP-8) resolution loop — a mis-referenced blocking plan gate degrades to a skipped dispatch instead of failing closed.
Drops config wrapperPath resolution so rung 2 never wins; reader/writer agreement with install-gh-bot.sh silently breaks.
Stops recording seen ids, so repo-unique claim ids are no longer enforced and a duplicate severity waiver lints clean.
Deletes the lanes[].name required check: no invalid fixture asserts it and every valid fixture still passes.
Swapped operand in cache_hit_rate: the reported rate silently measures cache CREATION against the read+creation denominator.
Drops the ^ anchor from the .claude/ alternatives, so a mid-path .claude/ segment (apps/web/.claude/x.mjs) is misclassified as inert and skips the verify suite.
Duplicate AC rows in a structure-only run go unreported, so a plan can claim the same criterion twice.
Gate-body regression: on typecheck failure the hook silently ALLOWS the commit.
Preflight reads the unfiltered issue list instead of the queue, so its reported queue head is not the queue head.
Escalates PARTIAL baseline staleness from warn to FAIL — a false-red class rather than a fail-open one.
Narrows the tolerant field fallback: reviewers that put the claim in .title score as MISSED.
Loosened single-target derivation: a DUAL-target run silently verifies only the first repo's command table.

Drops the first SEAM_SCRUB token (order is load-bearing — the sed consumes the trailing pipe): SECOND_SHIFT_CONFIG leaks into every configured lane's child again (#83/#34). check-lockstep-pairs.sh stays green under this mutant (dropping one token from the subset side keeps it a valid subset) — verifyctl-selftest.sh's (v32) is the sole killer.

column3: s#^ +append_line "\$\(now_iso\) \| milestone-3 \| skipped \| no verifying lane configured.*$##
column4: Deletes the zero-lane opt-out's AUDIT record while leaving its stdout notice intact: a lean run that verified nothing still tells the operator so, but leaves reconcile nothing to read. The generic tier cannot reach this guard at all — its sites are cmp-eq ordinal 11 and logic ordinal 67, and K_BUDGET=2 stops the site loop far below both — so these two rows are the automated lane's only reach into it.

column3: s#fail_milestone 3 "no verifying lane configured#fail_milestone 2 "no verifying lane configured#
column4: Re-keys the zero-lane red to milestone 2: the attempt/fix-budget counter is charged to a milestone that did not fail and the operator is sent to fix the wrong one. Doubly unreachable by the generic tier — no operator (fail-open/cmp-eq/cmp-z/logic/detector/default) mutates a bare integer literal at any K.
A ledger row with a blank Decision cell lints clean, so an undisclosed decision passes the gate that exists to surface it.
Rounding regression: the emit deadline's ceil becomes a floor, shortening every reviewer's budget by one turn at the boundary.
Breaks EXECUTOR_MODEL resolution in the mutation-gate tier check, so mutation-executor tier drift goes unguarded.
Drops the preflight-mode failure, so an alias heading warns but never blocks at --preflight.
Files in SUBDIRECTORIES of review-context/ start getting flagged — a false-positive class the depth limit exists to prevent.
Drops the reviewers.remove subtraction from the effective registry, so a removed reviewer is still treated as registered.
Deletes the hook-mode standalone fail-open, so un-onboarded repos get their commits denied again.

column3: s#printf 'note: dev-pipeline plugin not resolved#exit 1; printf 'note: dev-pipeline plugin not resolved#
column4: Makes the sibling-absent path fail CLOSED instead of skip-with-note, breaking the standalone review-toolkit adoption contract.
Inverts the text-fallback marketplace-ref branch: only JSON marketplace lists are ever injected, so the text path is unexercised.
Deletes the Makefile fallback, so make-based repos onboard with all-undetected commands.
Drops the numeric sort flags: fixture tags order identically lexicographically, and only a double-digit component (v10 vs v9) exposes it.
Drops the pinned ref from the contents API URL, so the lockfile silently records default-branch versions — the exact defect the script header exists to prevent.
Silent success on input that was all H1/comment lines, so an empty scaffold reads as a successful one.
Typos the fetched lint path: every stubbed gh ignores its arguments, so the literal is never validated end to end.
Drops the jq-absent guard; with jq missing the behavior is accidentally identical (silent, exit 0), so nothing observes the difference.
Accepts a mid-line mention as a trailer: no fixture has a non-trailer 'Changelog' mention, so all cases still pass.

column3: s#^    if \[ ! -d "\$dir" \]; then$#    if false; then#
column4: Removes the UNLOCATABLE hard-error branch, so a moved tree passes vacuously instead of failing loudly.
Weakens normalize() to strip ALL whitespace instead of collapsing runs, so blocks differing only in token boundaries compare equal.
Patch-tiebreak operand swap in ver_max: no fixture compares versions equal in major and minor but differing in patch.
Drops a guarded file from PROJECT_FILEWIDE, silently narrowing the .project/ leg's coverage.

Deletes the entry attestation ROW while leaving cmd_entry's stdout confirmation intact: the operator is told the run attested and every later reader finds nothing, which is #416's exact failure — a precondition that holds and leaves no evidence. The stdout half is what makes this survivable-looking, so the killer must read the file, not the output.

Narrows the build-role precondition to `claim` alone, leaving 1..5, `all` and `delta` unguarded. A run that starts at a milestone — every resume, and both runs that motivated #416 — walks straight through, while a claim-first run still reds, so a suite testing only the happy ordering stays green.

column3: s#if grep -qF "\| entry \| ledger=" "\$PROGRESS_FILE"#if grep -qvF "| entry | ledger=" "$PROGRESS_FILE"#
column4: Inverts the entry-attestation arm: an attested run reds and an unattested one passes. Catches a fixture that only ever exercises one side of the arm — the direction a paired red/green case exists to pin.

column3: s#bad "\$pname disabled in \$\(basename "\$f"\) while dev-pipeline#warn "$pname disabled in $(basename "$f") while dev-pipeline#
column4: Demotes the broken-lean-lane FAIL back to a warn. The message is unchanged and doctor still prints it, so only the EXIT CODE moves — which is the whole of D-7, and exactly the softening the receipt names as the failure mode to refuse.
